text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that appears immediately on keyboard navigation. This ensures keyboard users can always see where they are, meeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA. The trade-off is visual clutter for mouse users, but it’s minimal and outweighed by accessibility needs.

name: Reader
text: The single high-contrast ring still forces sighted keyboard users to parse a moving target every time they tab—fatigue and cognitive load spike. Instead, keep the ring but make it appear instantly *and* stay visible until the next tab, then fade only after 5 seconds of inactivity. Test with 3 keyboard users on slow machines; if any struggle to track focus, revert to a static ring.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that appears instantly on keyboard navigation and stays visible for 5 seconds of inactivity before fading. This balances immediate visibility for keyboard users with reduced visual clutter for mouse users. The trade-off is a slight delay in fading, but it prevents the fatigue of a moving target while still meeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA.

name: Reader
text: The 5-second delay still risks missing the user’s next tab—especially on slow machines where the ring may fade mid-navigation. Instead, tie the fade to the *next* keyboard event: the ring appears instantly, stays until the next tab, then fades only after 2 seconds of inactivity. Settle it by testing with 3 keyboard users on low-end hardware—if any miss the ring mid-tab, the alternative wins.

name: Access
text:
DECISION: Ship a **high-contrast focus ring that appears instantly on keyboard navigation and stays visible until the next tab, then fades after 2 seconds of inactivity**.

Result: A toggleable, WCAG 2.2 Level AA-compliant focus ring with no visual clutter for mouse users. Owner: accessibility-w1.
